Welcome to Talavera Infant School
Talavera Infant School is based on Gun Hill in Aldershot, Hampshire. We provide education for approximately 270 children from ages 4-7 years, from a range of backgrounds, the majority being Military.
At Talavera Infant School we want the best for every child. We believe that however long a child is with us, if it is one term or three years it is important that they make good progress and are equipped for the next part of their education. The staff work hard to make sure children feel that they belong and are part of a caring community. We have high expectations for our children and believe that every child can be successful. Our curriculum is based around topics which we hope excite and motivate the children to learn and encourage parents to participate in their child’s learning.
Prospective Parents 2026
We would like to welcome you to attend one of our parent tours, so that you can find out more about Talavera Infant School. We ask all prospective parents to contact the school office on 01252 323137 to book an appointment. There is further information about starting school under the parents tab in the website menu.,

Hampshire Music Service Sing Up
This is a summary of how our school delivers music education to all our pupils across three areas – curriculum music, co-curricular provision and musical experiences – and what changes we are planning in future years. This information is to help pupils and parents or carers understand what our school offers and who we work with to support our pupils’ music education.
Part A: Curriculum music
This is about what we teach in lesson time, how much time is spent teaching music and any music qualifications or awards that pupils can achieve.
Children in each class have weekly music lessons between 30 and 60 minutes long throughout the academic year.
Our music curriculum follows the Sing Up scheme of work which has been carefully developed to provide a curriculum which encourages and supports singing and musical learning with children and young people so that they:
We believe that taking part in musical activity brings about positive benefits for all individuals. Singing specifically supports learning, personal and social development, promotes health and well-being and bonds communities of people like no other activity
Learn to sing well and enjoy singing
Develop musical skills and understanding
Part B: Co-curricular music
This is about opportunities for pupils to sing and play music, outside of lesson time, including choirs, ensembles and bands, and how pupils can make progress in music beyond the core curriculum.
Outside of lesson time, Talavera Infant School offers KS1 children the opportunity to take part in a singing and music club. This is free to children and run by teachers in the school with a passion for music and singing.
We have been fortunate to have a local music company perform to the children and offer local lessons outside school should children wish to learn an instrument.
Part C: Musical experiences
This is about all the other musical events and opportunities that we organise, such as singing in assembly and concerts and shows.
The children in Year R enjoy accessing music though play and also have plenty of opportunities to learn songs and rhymes. As children learn and explore making music and singing, they begin to develop their performance skills both individually and in groups. The playground stage provides an exciting area for children to sing, act and perform and is used by all children during break times.
Children in KS1 take part in singing assembly every week and really enjoy learning new songs and singing together. We have recently introduced a selection of songs with actions to provide a more inclusive experience for children who are non-verbal or have additional needs.
At Christmas, the children rehearse and perform a Christmas play for the parents to come and see. This provides the children with the opportunity to demonstrate the performance skills they have been learning in class and be part of something they can really be proud of.
We also take part in an annual Community Carol Concert and the Year 2 children are invited to learn a carol and perform at this wonderful event. This gives them an opportunity to develop their performance skills and show how proud they are to represent our school.
In the future
This is about what the school is planning for subsequent years.
We are planning to use singing more consistently as a tool to support the children’s transition through the school. Following on from our ambition to use consistent visual support and language throughout the school, it is our aim to develop songs and singing to support daily routines.
We will endeavour to provide the children with exposure to high quality, live musical experiences in and out of school where possible.
We are also looking to explore further the significance of cultural music with our community. Our children and their families represent many cultural backgrounds and we would love to encourage opportunities for this to be shared in school.

Breakfast and After School Club
Breakfast Club is the perfect way to kick start your child’s day! As well as a range of cereals, toast and fresh fruit on offer, your child will also take part in an exciting activity each morning. These activities include team games, arts and crafts, board games and challenges led by our sports provider, TS coaching!
Where does the breakfast club take place?
Breakfast Club is held in the Meadow at the Infant school, through the grey door on the playground.
What happens after Breakfast Club?
At the end of the session the pupils are escorted to their classrooms where they are signed in by their respective teachers.
Payment Terms & Conditions
Please complete the booking form on line. However you may use the service without a prior booking as long as payment is made to a TS member of staff on the day of attendance. All places are accepted unless TS Coaching inform you otherwise. TS Coaching are unable to issue credit notes or refunds due to a school closure or cancellation of any session by the school. The only exception would be an inset day where a credit note will be issued. For full terms and conditions and online booking please visit
https://togetherinsport.com/
After School Care Provision:
Talavera Infant School run the after school provision.The provision runs every day after school from 3.10pm – 5.45pm and takes place in the Meadow. The children enjoy a variety of extra curricular activities along with arts and crafts. Booking is via the Arbor parental portal and the cost is £12 per session. If you need any assistance with booking please contact the school office on 01252 323137.

In This Section
Early Years Curriculum​
In our Early Years Foundation Stage, children, relationships and language sit at the heart of everything we do. We believe that young children learn best through meaningful, real-life experiences, rich talk and purposeful play, supported by warm, responsive adults who know them well.
Developing communication and language is a key priority within our Early Years curriculum. We create language-rich environments where children are encouraged to listen, talk, ask questions and share ideas throughout the day. Through stories, songs, role play, exploration and first-hand experiences, children are introduced to new vocabulary and supported to use language confidently as they learn, play and build friendships.
Strong personal, social and emotional development underpins all learning. We help children to feel safe, valued and secure, enabling them to form positive relationships, manage their emotions and develop independence. Working and playing alongside others supports children to grow in empathy, cooperation and respect.
Alongside this, we place a strong emphasis on developing the foundational skills that prepare children for successful learning in Year 1. This includes a clear focus on early phonics to support reading and writing, as well as the development of gross and fine motor skills. Through carefully planned physical activities, play and practical experiences, children build strength, coordination and control, supporting their readiness for handwriting and wider learning.
Through a balance of adult-led and child-initiated learning, we nurture confident, curious and happy learners who are well prepared socially, emotionally and academically for the transition into Year 1.
The Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum consists of the Prime Areas of Communication and Language, Physical Development and Personal, Social and Emotional Development, and the Specific Areas of Literacy, Mathematics, Understand the World and Expressive Arts and Design.
Communication and language development involves giving children opportunities to experience a rich language environment; to develop their confidence and skills in expressing themselves; and to speak and listen in a range of situations.
Physical development involves providing opportunities for young children to be active and interactive; and to develop their co-ordination, control, and movement. Children must also be helped to understand the importance of physical activity, and to make healthy choices in relation to food.
Personal, social and emotional development involves helping children to develop a positive sense of themselves, and others; to form positive relationships and develop respect for others; to develop social skills and learn how to manage their feelings; to understand appropriate behaviour in groups; and to have confidence in their own abilities.
Literacy development involves encouraging children to link sounds and letters and to begin to read and write. Children must be given access to a wide range of reading materials (books, poems, and other written materials) to ignite their interest.
Mathematics involves providing children with opportunities to develop and improve their skills in counting, understanding and using numbers, calculating simple addition and subtraction problems; and to describe shapes, spaces, and measures.
Understanding the world involves guiding children to make sense of their physical world and their community through opportunities to explore, observe and find out about people, places, technology and the environment.
Expressive arts and design involves enabling children to explore and play with a wide range of media and materials, as well as providing opportunities and encouragement for sharing their thoughts, ideas and feelings through a variety of activities in art, music, movement, dance, role-play, and design and technology.
At Talavera Infant School we plan the children’s learning through their own interests and key topics. In the Early Years this year we have covered the following topics:
Please see a copy of our curriculum overviews for Early Years. Further information about what the children will be learning in each topic will be provided in the half termly newsletter.
Autumn 1 – All About Me
Autumn 2 – Celebrations
Spring 2 – Superstars
Summer 1 – Gardens and Growing
Summer 2 – Out and about

In This Section
Literacy and Maths Curriculum
Literacy
Our curriculum is designed using key quality texts to ensure children develop a good understanding of literacy. It is focused on developing the children’s vocabulary and knowledge of story structures to ensure the children are able to retell and create their own stories both orally and written. The reading curriculum is focused on developing the skills of reasoning, fluency, accuracy and understanding.
Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised 2021: Programme progression Reception and Year 1 overviewsThis programme overview shows the progression of GPCs and tricky words that we teach term-by-term. The progression has been organised so that children are taught from the simple to more complex GPCs, as well as taking into accountthe frequency of their occurrence in the most commonly encountered words. All the graphemes taught are practised in words, sentences, and later on, in fully decodable books. Children review and revise GPCs and words, daily, weekly andacross terms and years, in order to move this knowledge into their long term memory.Children need to learn to read as quickly as reasonably possible, so they can move from learning to read, to reading to learn, giving them access to the treasure house of reading. Our expectations of progression are aspirational yet achievable if schools maintain pace, practice and participation by all children. Children who are not keeping-up with their peers will be given additional practice immediately through keep-up sessions. A breakdown of the content covered in ‘Little Wandle Letters and Sounds’ can be seen below:
Phonic knowledge and skills
Autumn 1 – Phase 2 Graphemes
s a t p i n m d g o c k ck e u r h b f l
Tricky words: is I the
Autumn 2 – Phase 2 Graphemes
ff ll ss j v w x y z zz qu ch sh th ng nk• words with –s /s/ added at the end (hats sits)• words ending –s /z/ (his) and with –s /z/ added at the end(bags)
Tricky words: put* pull* full* as and has his her go no to into she push* he of we me be
Spring term – Phase 3

Review Phase 3• longer words, including those with double letters• words with –s /z/ in the middle• words with –es /z/ at the end• words with –s /s/ and /z/ at the end
Tricky words: was you they my by all are sure pure
Summer Term -Phase 4
Short vowels with adjacent consonants• CVCC CCVC CCVCC CCCVC CCCVCC• longer words and compound words• words ending in suffixes:–ing, –ed /t/, –ed /id/ /ed/, –est
Phase 3 long vowel graphemes with adjacent consonants• CVCC CCVC CCCVC CCV CCVCC• words ending in suffixes:–ing, –ed /t/, –ed /id/ /ed/, –ed /d/ –er, –est• longer words and compound words
Tricky words: said so have like some come love do were here little says there when what one out today
Phase Five (Throughout Year 1)
Now we move on to the “complex code”. Children learn more graphemes for the phonemes which they already know, plus different ways of pronouncing the graphemes they already know.
‘Little Wandle Letters and Sounds’ provides comprehensive guides and videos for parents to support everyone in helping the children learn to read at Talavera Infant School. Our core reading books are Big Cat- Letters and Sounds, we have many other phonic books to support the children in learning to read. As well as 1:1 reading with an adult, children read in small groups with each child reading the same book. In this way school staff can teach a specific skill most effectively. We value the 1:1 time that parents can spend reading with their children, and we expect children to read a minimum of three times a week at home and ideally every day.
Teachers use ‘Little Wandle Letters and Sounds’ to introduce the formation of letters in handwriting and children learn how to write in print from YR and are taught to join their handwriting in Y2. Many children aren’t ready to write with a pencil when they start school so we encourage them to practise their letter shapes by writing in the air or in sand which helps to develop their arm muscles as well as helping them to learn letter shapes.
Regular practising of handwriting throughout years one and two helps children to master the skill of cursive letter formation. Spellings are often practised at the same time as handwriting.
The new national curriculum has an increased focus on the correct use of grammar, and on children knowing the correct terminology for grammatical terms.
For further information about the English curriculum and the key quality texts please select the buttons below
Maths
Throughout the school there is a focus on learning maths using practical objects, then pictorial recording before teaching children symbolic recording. We encourage children to explain how they arrived at a specific answer, and compare different ways of calculating to decide which is the most effective. This ‘mathematical reasoning’ is a significant part of the maths curriculum and enables us to find out whether children really understand what they are doing and why. In Years 1 and 2 we follow the National Curriculum 2014, which ensures children have mastered all of the basic mathematical skills and can use them fluently before moving on and working with greater numbers. Throughout Years 1 and 2 the class teachers frequently set additional maths homework which encourages the children to practise the many skills to help them achieve fluency.

In This Section
Personal, Social, Health and Relationships Education
At our school, we are committed to supporting children’s personal development, wellbeing and emotional health. Through our PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic) education and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), we help children develop the knowledge, skills and values they need to lead happy, healthy and safe lives.
Our PSHE curriculum helps children build positive relationships, understand their feelings, develop resilience and learn how to make responsible choices.
We teach PSHE using the Jigsaw programme, a whole-school approach that supports children’s personal, social and emotional development.
The programme is organised into six themes which are taught across the year:
• Being Me in My World – understanding belonging, responsibilities and feeling valued
• Celebrating Difference – respecting similarities and differences between people
• Dreams and Goals – setting goals and learning about perseverance
•Healthy Me – learning about physical and mental health and healthy lifestyles
• Relationships – building positive friendships and understanding how to treat others kindly
• Changing Me – learning about growth and change in an age-appropriate way
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is taught as part of the Jigsaw programme and focuses on friendships, families, respect, and keeping ourselves safe.
You can view more detail about what is taught in each year group through our PSHE Medium Term Plan.
We also use myHappymind, a programme that supports children’s mental health and emotional wellbeing.
Through engaging lessons and activities, children learn about how their brain works and develop important skills to support their wellbeing. The programme helps children to:
• recognise and celebrate their character strengths
• practise gratitude and appreciation
• build confidence and self-esteem
• understand and regulate their emotions
• develop positive habits for wellbeing
These skills help children become more resilient, confident and ready to learn.
Assemblies and School Values
Our assemblies play an important role in supporting children’s personal development. Through stories, discussions and shared learning, assemblies help children deepen their understanding of PSHE themes and explore important life values.
Assemblies are closely linked to our school values:
These values help guide children in how they treat others, approach their learning and take pride in themselves and their achievements.
Useful Information
Parents can find more detailed information in the documents below:
• PSHE and RSE Medium Term Plan
• PSHE and RSE Policy
If you have any questions about our PSHE or RSE curriculum, please contact the school office or ask your child’s class teacher

In This Section
British Values​
Promoting British Values at Talavera Infant School
The Department for Education states that “schools should promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
At Talavera Infant School these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy is embedded at the school. Pupils are always listened to by adults and are taught to listen carefully and with concern to each other, respecting the right of every individual to have their opinions and voices heard. Pupils also have the opportunity to air their opinions and ideas through our School Council and regular questionnaires. The elections of the School Council members are based on pupil votes, reflecting our British electoral system and demonstrating democracy in action.
The importance of laws whether they are those that govern the class, the school or the country, are consistently reinforced. Our school has clear Golden rules and a code of conduct which are deeply embedded in our work every day. These are reinforced through carefully planned assemblies and lessons. Each class discusses and sets its own class charter as part of our PHSE curriculum ‘Jigsaw’. The class charters are clearly understood by all and are necessary to ensure that every class member is able to learn in a safe and ordered environment. Through PHSE, our pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for our pupils to make choices safely, through the provision of a safe environment and an empowering education. Our pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely; examples of this can be clearly seen in our e-safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it is through choice of challenge, how they record their learning or participation in our extra- curricular activities, our pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
Respect is embedded through our PSHE curriculum and Collective Worship programme. The pupils know and understand that it is expected and imperative that respect is shown to everyone, whatever differences we may have and to everything, however big or small. Respect forms part of the school’s Vision and aims and underpins our work every day both in and out of the classroom.
Tolerance of Those With Different Faiths And Beliefs:
Talavera Infant School enhances pupils’ understanding of different faiths and beliefs through religious education studies, our PSHE curriculum and Collective Worship programme. We welcome visitors to enrich and extend the children’s understanding of different faiths and beliefs. Through this our pupils gain an enhanced understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society.

Camouflage Club
Camouflage Club is run by school staff to help support children who have a parent or family member in the armed forces who has, or is about to be, deployed abroad OR extended training away from home. It is held once a week on a Friday afternoon. We have a 2 week rota in operation, with Reception Year and Year 1 on week 1 and Year 2 on week 2.
The children have opportunities to record messages, pictures and parcels as well as keep a scrap book to use as a discussion point when their loved one returns.
If your child would like to attend Camouflage Club, complete the form below and return to your child’s class teacher. Please let us know if any contact details change so that we can make sure that the children’s messages reach the correct person.

Engage, Inspire, Achieve
At Talavera Infant School we want the best for every child. We believe that however long a child is with us, if it is one term or three years it is important that they make good progress and are equipped for the next part of their education. The staff work hard to make sure children feel that they belong and are part of a caring community. We have high expectations for our children and believe that every child can be successful. Our curriculum is based around topics which we hope excite and motivate the children to learn and encourage parents to participate in their child’s learning.
